pairs: In lapide luteo lapidatus est piger:
The lazy man is pelted with a dirty stone,
et omnes loquentur super aspernationem illius.
and all will speak about his rejection.
De stercore boum lapidatus est piger:
The lazy man is pelted with the dung of oxen,
et omnis qui tetigerit eum excutiet manus.
and all who touch him will brush off their hands.
Confusio patris est de filio indisciplinato:
An undisciplined son is the shame of his father,
filia autem in deminoratione fiet.
but an undisciplined daughter will be to his degradation.
Filia prudens hæreditas viro suo:
A prudent daughter brings an inheritance to her husband.
nam quæ confundit, in contumeliam fit genitoris.
But she who causes shame will be a disgrace to him who conceived her.
Patrem et virum confundit audax,
She who is bold shames her father and her husband,
et ab impiis non minorabitur:
and she will not be less offensive to the impious.
ab utrisque autem inhonorabitur.
For she will be held in dishonor by both.
Musica in luctu importuna narratio:
An untimely explanation is like music in a time of mourning.
flagella et doctrina in omni tempore sapientia.
But the sharp correction and doctrine of wisdom are ever timely.
Qui docet fatuum, quasi qui conglutinat testam.
Whoever teaches the foolish is like someone who glues together a broken pot.
Qui narrat verbum non audienti, quasi qui excitat dormientem de gravi somno.
Whoever explains a word to one who is not listening is like someone who suddenly awakens a sleeping person from a deep sleep.
Cum dormiente loquitur qui enarrat stulto sapientiam:
Whoever explains wisdom to the senseless is like one speaking to a sleeping person.
et in fine narrationis dicit:
And at the end of the explanation, he says:
Quis est hic?
“Who is this?”
Supra mortuum plora,
Weep over the dead,
defecit enim lux ejus:
for his light has failed.
et supra fatuum plora,
And weep over the foolish,
defecit enim sensus.
for his understanding has failed.
Modicum plora super mortuum,
Weep only a little over the dead,
quoniam requievit:
for he is at rest.
nequissimi enim nequissima vita super mortem fatui.
But the wicked life of a wicked fool is worse than death.
Luctus mortui septem dies:
The mourning for the dead is seven days;
fatui autem
but for the foolish and the impious,
et impii omnes dies vitæ illorum.
it is all the days of their life.
Cum stulto ne multum loquaris,
You should not talk at length with the foolish,
et cum insensato ne abieris.
and you should not go with the senseless.
Serva te ab illo,
Keep yourself from him,
ut non molestiam habeas,
so that you may not have problems,
et non coinquinaberis peccato illius.
and so that you will not be polluted by his sin.
Deflecte ab illo,
Turn away from him,
et invenies requiem,
and you will find rest,
et non acediaberis in stultitia illius.
and you will not be discouraged by his foolishness.
Super plumbum quid gravabitur?
What is heavier than lead?
et quod illi aliud nomen quam fatuus?
And what else can he be called but foolish?
Arenam,
Sand,
et salem,
and salt,
et massam ferri facilius est ferre quam hominem imprudentem,
and an iron weight are each easier to bear than an imprudent man,
et fatuum,
who is both foolish
et impium.
and impious.
Loramentum ligneum colligatum in fundamento ædificii non dissolvetur,
A bundle of wood strapped together in the foundation of a building will not be loosened.
sic et cor confirmatum in cogitatione consilii.
And similar is the heart that has been strengthened by thoughtful counsel.
Cogitatus sensati in omni tempore metu non depravabitur.
The thoughts of one who is understanding will not be corrupted by fear in any situation.
Sicut pali in excelsis,
Just as chaff in a high place,
et cæmenta sine impensa posita,
or a wall made of mortar without stones set within,
contra faciem venti non permanebunt:
will not continue against the face of the wind,
sic et cor timidum in cogitatione stulti contra impetum timoris non resistet.
so also a timid heart, and the thoughts of the senseless, will not withstand the forcefulness of fear.
Sicut cor trepidum in cogitatione fatui omni tempore non metuet,
Despite a cowardly heart,
sic
the thoughts of the foolish will not fear any situation;
et qui in præceptis Dei permanet semper.
yet neither will one who continues always in the precepts of God.
Pungens oculum deducit lacrimas,
He who jabs an eye produces tears.
et qui pungit cor profert sensum.
And he who jabs the heart produces understanding.
Mittens lapidem in volatilia, dejiciet illa:
He who throws a stone at birds will drive them away.
sic et qui conviciatur amico, dissolvit amicitiam.
So also, he who accuses his friend dissolves the friendship.
Ad amicum etsi produxeris gladium,
But if you have drawn a sword against a friend,
non desperes:
you should not despair;
est enim regressus. Ad amicum
for there may be a way back.
si aperueris os triste,
If you have opened a harsh mouth against a friend,
non timeas:
you should not fear;
est enim concordatio:
for there may be a reconciliation.
excepto convitio, et improperio,
However, if there are accusations,
et superbia,
or abuse, or arrogance,
et mysterii revelatione, et plaga dolosa:
or the revealing of secrets, or a wound from deceitfulness,
in his omnibus effugiet amicus.
in all these cases, a friend will flee away.
Fidem posside cum amico in paupertate illius,
Hold to faithfulness with a friend in his poverty,
ut et in bonis illius læteris.
so that you may also rejoice in his prosperity.
In tempore tribulationis illius permane illi fidelis,
In the time of his tribulation,
ut
remain faithful to him,
et in hæreditate illius cohæres sis.
so that you may also be an heir with him in his inheritance.
Ante ignem camini vapor et fumus ignis inaltatur:
Just as the steam from an oven,
sic et ante sanguinem maledicta,
or the smoke from a fire,
et contumeliæ,
rises up before a flame,
et minæ.
so also do curses and insults and threats rise up before bloodshed.
Amicum salutare non confundar,
I shall not be ashamed to greet a friend,
a facie illius non me abscondam:
nor shall I hide myself from his face.
et si mala mihi evenerint per illum,
And if misfortunes befall me because of him,
sustinebo.
I will endure.
Omnis qui audiet cavebit se ab eo.
Anyone who hears of this will be wary around him.
Quis dabit ori meo custodiam,
Who will provide a keeper for my mouth,
et super labia mea signaculum certum,
and a reliable seal over my lips,
ut non cadam ab ipsis,
so that I may not fall because of them,
et lingua mea perdat me?
and so that my tongue does not destroy me?
